evidence.point: The approved AI tools for staff use within the organization are the enterprise AI assistant integrated with the document platform and the enterprise chat service with data retention switched off. Consumer AI services, browser extensions, and personal accounts are not approved for work purposes.
evidence.citation: Aurora Institute AI Use Policy, Approved tools

evidence.point: Restricted information may not be used with approved external chat services or any AI tool that sends data outside the Institute's environment. Restricted information can only be processed by models hosted inside the Institute's private cloud after a data protection review. The use of restricted information with AI tools is subject to risk-level approvals: minimal-risk cases are approved by the AI Office, limited-risk cases require agreement from the business owner and Information Security team, and high-risk cases (e.g., involving individual decisions or restricted information) require approval from the Digital Governance Board.
evidence.citation: Data Classification and Handling Guide, Using classified information with AI tools; AI Use Case Intake Procedure, Risk levels and approval

evidence.point: AI prompts and outputs are not considered official records by default. However, when an AI output is used in a decision or publication, the final version becomes part of the related record and is subject to the retention period applicable to that record type. Retention periods are counted from the end of the calendar year in which the record was closed, and records under a legal hold are retained until the hold is lifted.
evidence.citation: Aurora Institute Records Retention Schedule, AI prompts and outputs; Aurora Institute Records Retention Schedule, How to read this schedule
